description: A Telegram bot that allows users to create, edit, and export presentations using natural language and voice input, powered by AI.

general_info.title: Create Presentation from Text and Voice
general_info.description: Users can create a new presentation by sending a text message or a voice message to the Telegram bot. Voice messages are transcribed automatically. The AI processes the input and generates an initial set of slides.

goal_and_context.goal: Allow users to quickly bootstrap a presentation by describing its topic and content in natural language or via voice.
goal_and_context.context: This is the primary entry point for the product. Users interact with the Telegram bot, send a prompt describing the desired presentation, and the system generates a structured slide deck.

actors_and_roles.role: Initiates presentation creation by sending text or voice input via Telegram.
Receives user input, forwards it to the backend service.
Processes the input, calls the AI model, and stores the generated presentation.
Generates slide content based on the user prompt.

business_rules.description: Each user may have multiple presentations stored simultaneously.
Voice messages must be transcribed to text before processing.
The AI-generated presentation must contain between 3 and 20 slides.
Each presentation must be associated with the Telegram user ID of the creator.

acceptance_criteria.title: Create presentation from text
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is in a chat with the bot
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends a text message describing a presentation topic
acceptance_criteria.then: The system generates a presentation with structured slides and confirms creation to the user

acceptance_criteria.title: Create presentation from voice
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is in a chat with the bot
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends a voice message describing a presentation topic
acceptance_criteria.then: The system transcribes the voice message, generates a presentation, and confirms creation to the user

acceptance_criteria.title: Handle empty or unintelligible input
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is in a chat with the bot
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends an empty message or an unintelligible voice message
acceptance_criteria.then: The system responds with a helpful error message asking the user to try again

non_functional_requirements.description: Presentation generation must complete within 30 seconds.
Voice transcription accuracy must be at least 90% for clear audio.
The system must support at least 100 concurrent presentation generation requests.

test_cases.title: Text input generates presentation
steps: Send a text message: 'Create a presentation about machine learning'
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with confirmation and a summary of generated slides.

test_cases.title: Voice input generates presentation
steps: Send a voice message describing a presentation topic
test_cases.expected_result: Bot transcribes the voice, generates slides, and responds with confirmation.

test_cases.title: Empty input is rejected
steps: Send an empty text message to the bot
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with an error message prompting the user to provide content.

general_info.title: Auto Slide Structuring
general_info.description: The system automatically structures the AI-generated content into well-organized slides with titles, bullet points, and logical flow.

goal_and_context.goal: Ensure that generated presentations have a professional structure with clear slide titles, concise bullet points, and a logical narrative flow.
goal_and_context.context: Raw AI output needs to be parsed and structured into a slide format. Each slide should have a title and body content. The system applies formatting rules and content limits per slide.

actors_and_roles.role: Parses AI output and applies structuring rules.
Generates raw content that is then structured into slides.

business_rules.description: Each slide must have a title of no more than 100 characters.
Each slide body must contain no more than 6 bullet points.
The first slide must be a title slide with the presentation topic.
The last slide should be a summary or conclusion slide.

acceptance_criteria.title: Slides are structured with titles and bullets
acceptance_criteria.given: The AI has generated raw content for a presentation
acceptance_criteria.when: The backend processes the AI output
acceptance_criteria.then: Each slide has a title and a list of bullet points, with a title slide first and a conclusion slide last

acceptance_criteria.title: Slide count is within limits
acceptance_criteria.given: The AI has generated content
acceptance_criteria.then: The total number of slides is between 3 and 20

non_functional_requirements.description: Slide structuring must complete within 5 seconds after AI content generation.
Structuring rules must be configurable without code changes.

test_cases.title: Slides have correct structure
steps: Generate a presentation from a text prompt
test_cases.expected_result: Each slide has a non-empty title (max 100 chars) and body with up to 6 bullet points.

test_cases.title: First and last slides are correct
steps: Check the first and last slides
test_cases.expected_result: First slide is a title slide; last slide is a summary/conclusion.

general_info.title: Slide Navigation Widget in Telegram
general_info.description: Users can navigate through their presentation slides directly within the Telegram chat using inline keyboard buttons (Previous, Next, slide number indicator).

goal_and_context.goal: Provide an intuitive in-chat navigation experience so users can review each slide without leaving Telegram.
goal_and_context.context: After a presentation is generated or loaded, the bot displays the current slide content and provides navigation buttons. The slide content is shown as a formatted text message.

actors_and_roles.role: Navigates through slides using inline buttons.
Renders slide content and inline keyboard for navigation.
Serves slide data for the requested slide index.

business_rules.description: The Previous button must be hidden on the first slide.
The Next button must be hidden on the last slide.
The slide indicator must show the format 'Slide X of Y'.
Navigation must update the existing message rather than sending a new one.

acceptance_criteria.title: Navigate to next slide
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is viewing slide 1 of a 5-slide presentation
acceptance_criteria.when: The user taps the Next button
acceptance_criteria.then: The message updates to show slide 2 with the indicator 'Slide 2 of 5'

acceptance_criteria.title: Navigate to previous slide
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is viewing slide 3 of a 5-slide presentation
acceptance_criteria.when: The user taps the Previous button
acceptance_criteria.then: The message updates to show slide 2 with the indicator 'Slide 2 of 5'

acceptance_criteria.title: First slide hides Previous button
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is viewing slide 1
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the Next button is displayed

acceptance_criteria.title: Last slide hides Next button
acceptance_criteria.given: The user is viewing the last slide
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the Previous button is displayed

non_functional_requirements.description: Slide navigation must respond within 1 second of button press.
Slide content must be readable on mobile devices without horizontal scrolling.

test_cases.title: Next button navigates forward
test_cases.expected_result: Slide 2 is displayed with correct indicator.

test_cases.title: Previous button navigates backward
test_cases.expected_result: Slide 2 is displayed with correct indicator.

test_cases.title: Boundary buttons are hidden
steps: Navigate to last slide, check buttons
test_cases.expected_result: Previous is hidden on slide 1; Next is hidden on the last slide.

general_info.title: Edit Slides via Natural Language
general_info.description: Users can edit individual slides or the entire presentation by sending natural language instructions to the bot (e.g., 'Make slide 3 more concise', 'Add a slide about pricing').

goal_and_context.goal: Enable users to iteratively refine their presentations using conversational commands instead of manual editing.
goal_and_context.context: After generating a presentation, users often want to adjust content. This feature allows them to describe changes in plain language, and the AI applies the edits to the relevant slides.

actors_and_roles.role: Sends edit instructions in natural language.
Receives edit instructions and forwards them to the backend.
Identifies the target slides, calls the AI model with edit instructions, and updates the stored presentation.
Processes edit instructions and generates updated slide content.

business_rules.description: Edit commands must reference a valid presentation belonging to the user.
If the user references a specific slide number, it must exist in the presentation.
Adding a new slide must not exceed the maximum of 20 slides.
Deleting slides must not reduce the presentation below 3 slides.

acceptance_criteria.title: Edit a specific slide
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.then: Slide 3 is updated with more concise content and the user sees the updated slide

acceptance_criteria.title: Add a new slide
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends 'Add a slide about our team after slide 4'
acceptance_criteria.then: A new slide is inserted at position 5, and the presentation now has 6 slides

acceptance_criteria.title: Delete a slide
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.then: Slide 2 is removed, the presentation now has 4 slides, and slide numbers are recalculated

acceptance_criteria.title: Reject invalid slide reference
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot responds with an error indicating that slide 10 does not exist

non_functional_requirements.description: Slide edits must be applied within 15 seconds.
Failed edits must not corrupt the existing presentation data.

test_cases.title: Edit specific slide content
test_cases.expected_result: Slide 2 content is updated with more detail.

test_cases.title: Add a slide via natural language
test_cases.expected_result: Presentation now has 6 slides with the new slide added.

test_cases.title: Delete a slide via natural language
test_cases.expected_result: Presentation now has 4 slides.

test_cases.title: Cannot delete below minimum
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with an error that the presentation cannot have fewer than 3 slides.

general_info.title: View Slide Structure
general_info.description: Users can request an overview of the entire presentation structure, showing all slide titles and their positions in a compact list format.

goal_and_context.goal: Give users a bird's-eye view of their presentation to understand the overall flow and identify slides to edit.
goal_and_context.context: Before making edits, users need to see the full structure. This command returns a numbered list of slide titles.

actors_and_roles.role: Requests the presentation structure overview.
Formats and displays the structure as a numbered list.
Retrieves all slide titles for the active presentation.

business_rules.description: The structure view must show slide numbers and titles only.
If no active presentation exists, the bot must prompt the user to create one.

acceptance_criteria.title: View structure of existing presentation
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot responds with a numbered list of all 5 slide titles

acceptance_criteria.title: No active presentation
acceptance_criteria.given: The user does not have an active presentation
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot responds with a message prompting the user to create a presentation first

non_functional_requirements.description: Structure view must load within 2 seconds.

test_cases.title: Structure command returns slide list
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with numbered list of slide titles.

test_cases.title: Structure command with no presentation
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with prompt to create a presentation.

general_info.title: Confirm Final Version
general_info.description: Users can mark their presentation as finalized, locking it from further edits and making it available for export.

goal_and_context.goal: Provide a clear workflow step where users confirm they are satisfied with the presentation before exporting.
goal_and_context.context: Before generating HTML or PDF exports, users should confirm the final version. This prevents accidental exports of incomplete presentations.

actors_and_roles.role: Confirms the presentation is final.
Asks for confirmation and updates the presentation status.
Updates the presentation status to 'finalized' in the database.

business_rules.description: A finalized presentation cannot be edited unless the user explicitly unlocks it.
The bot must ask for explicit confirmation before finalizing (Yes/No buttons).
Only the presentation owner can finalize a presentation.

acceptance_criteria.title: Finalize presentation
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation in draft status
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends /finalize and confirms with Yes
acceptance_criteria.then: The presentation status is updated to 'finalized' and the bot confirms the action

acceptance_criteria.title: Cancel finalization
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has an active presentation in draft status
acceptance_criteria.when: The user sends /finalize and selects No
acceptance_criteria.then: The presentation remains in draft status

non_functional_requirements.description: Only the presentation owner can finalize or unlock a presentation.

test_cases.title: Finalize a presentation
test_cases.expected_result: Presentation is marked as finalized.

test_cases.title: Cancel finalization
test_cases.expected_result: Presentation remains in draft.

test_cases.title: Cannot edit finalized presentation
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with error that the presentation is finalized.

general_info.title: Generate HTML Presentation
general_info.description: Users can export their finalized presentation as a self-contained HTML file that can be viewed in any web browser as a slideshow.

goal_and_context.goal: Allow users to get a shareable, browser-viewable presentation file from their slide content.
goal_and_context.context: The HTML export uses a lightweight slideshow framework (e.g., Reveal.js) to render slides. The file is sent to the user as a document in Telegram.

actors_and_roles.role: Requests HTML export of the presentation.
Sends the generated HTML file as a document to the user.
Generates the HTML file from the presentation data using a template engine.

business_rules.description: Only finalized presentations can be exported to HTML.
The HTML file must be self-contained with embedded CSS and JS.
The generated HTML file size must not exceed 5 MB.

acceptance_criteria.title: Export finalized presentation to HTML
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has a finalized presentation
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot sends an HTML file as a document that can be opened in a browser as a slideshow

acceptance_criteria.title: Reject export of draft presentation
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has a presentation in draft status
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot responds with an error asking the user to finalize the presentation first

non_functional_requirements.description: HTML generation must complete within 10 seconds.
The HTML file must render correctly in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

test_cases.title: Export to HTML
test_cases.expected_result: An HTML file is received that opens as a slideshow in the browser.

test_cases.title: Reject export of draft
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with error to finalize first.

test_cases.title: HTML file is self-contained
test_cases.expected_result: The slideshow renders correctly without internet access.

general_info.title: Export to PDF
general_info.description: Users can export their finalized presentation as a PDF document with one slide per page.

goal_and_context.goal: Provide a universally compatible export format for printing and sharing presentations.
goal_and_context.context: PDF export converts the HTML presentation into a multi-page PDF document. Each slide becomes one page in landscape orientation.

actors_and_roles.role: Requests PDF export of the presentation.
Sends the generated PDF file as a document to the user.
Converts the presentation to PDF using a headless browser or PDF library.

business_rules.description: Only finalized presentations can be exported to PDF.
Each slide must occupy exactly one page in landscape orientation.
The PDF file size must not exceed 10 MB.

acceptance_criteria.title: Export finalized presentation to PDF
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has a finalized presentation with 5 slides
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot sends a 5-page PDF document with one slide per page

acceptance_criteria.title: Reject PDF export of draft presentation
acceptance_criteria.given: The user has a presentation in draft status
acceptance_criteria.then: The bot responds with an error asking the user to finalize the presentation first

non_functional_requirements.description: PDF generation must complete within 20 seconds.
PDF output must have a minimum resolution of 150 DPI.

test_cases.title: Export to PDF
test_cases.expected_result: A PDF file is received with one slide per page in landscape orientation.

test_cases.title: Reject PDF export of draft
test_cases.expected_result: Bot responds with error to finalize first.

test_cases.title: PDF page count matches slide count
test_cases.expected_result: PDF has exactly 7 pages.
